newsitem.title: PERU: Fujimori's approval rating slips in top Peru poll.
newsitem.headline: Fujimori's approval rating slips in top Peru poll.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori's approval rating fell four percentage points during March to 48 percent in the first week of April, according to leading pollster Apoyo SA.

The latest survey shows the president's rating rests at the same level as at the beginning of January and February, before it spiked in the first week of March due to the perception that Lima's hostage crisis would soon end peacefully.
Other pollsters, however, did not see any jump in Fujimori's popularity at the start of March, and have consistently shown his rating tucked just below 50 percent this year.

The almost four-month old siege at the Japanese ambassador's residence where Marxist rebels hold 72 VIP captives has hurt Fujimori in the polls, tarnishing his reputation as the man who virtually defeated Peru's rebels.

Sixty-two percent of respondents said they thought the siege could go on for another one to three months or even longer, according to the poll of 500 adults living in the capital Lima. The survey, published by local media, did not give a margin of error.

Commentators noted Apoyo conducted its survey before a scandal rocked Peru last week over the torture of a National Intelligence Service officer allegedly carried out by her own colleagues. The accusations could further hurt Fujimori's popularity owing to his perceived close links to the intelligence service, they said.
